note: Clinical concepts proposed from the literature. Every concept starts as a candidate. A candidate is never shown to a live answer and never enforced. It becomes enforced only when (1) its test cases pass at its current content (knowledge.py test) and (2) the clinical reviewer approves that exact content (knowledge.py review). Any edit to a concept's content after review returns it to candidate. Codes and thresholds are stated so they can be checked; the summary is in our own words.

concepts.name: CKD GFR categories (G1 to G5)
concepts.summary: KDIGO GFR categories in mL/min/1.73 m2: G1 90 or more, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 under 15; G1 and G2 are not CKD without markers of kidney damage. CKD stage 3 is eGFR 30-59 (G3a plus G3b). CKD requires the abnormality to last at least 3 months; KDIGO says not to assume chronicity from a single abnormal eGFR (it may be acute kidney injury). Agere's operational test (not KDIGO wording) is two eGFR results under 60 at least 90 days apart. Unless the question says otherwise, use each patient's eGFR results in the period; say whether a single result or two results 90 days apart were required.

retrieves: How many patients have stage 3 CKD by eGFR?
Patients with an eGFR under 30 in 2028
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'egfr' AND value_canonical >= 30 AND value_canonical < 60
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'egfr' AND value_canonical < 45
tests.check_question: How many patients had stage 3 CKD by eGFR in 2028?

concepts.name: Albuminuria categories (A1 to A3)
concepts.summary: KDIGO albuminuria categories by urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) in mg/g (mg/mmol): A1 under 30 (under 3), normal to mildly increased; A2 30-300 (3-30), moderately increased; A3 over 300 (over 30), severely increased. Albuminuria means uACR 30 mg/g or more. KDIGO advises reporting the ratio, not a urine albumin concentration (mg/L) alone. A2 was formerly called 'microalbuminuria', a general term KDIGO 2024 does not use.

measures.unit: mg/g (32294-1 is a unitless ratio: check its unit)

retrieves: How many patients with diabetes have albuminuria?
patients with a UACR over 300
ignores: How many flu shots were given in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'uacr' AND value_canonical >= 30
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'uacr' AND value_canonical > 20
tests.check_question: How many patients have albuminuria?

concepts.name: Acute kidney injury (KDIGO creatinine criteria)
concepts.triggers: acute kidney injury|\baki\b|acute renal failure|creatinine (?:rise|increase|jump)|kidney injur
concepts.summary: KDIGO AKI by serum creatinine: a rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more within 48 hours, or a rise to 1.5 times or more a baseline known or presumed to be from the prior 7 days; urine output under 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 hours also qualifies but is rarely in claims or lab tables. Stages by creatinine: 1 = 1.5-1.9 times baseline or +0.3; 2 = 2.0-2.9 times; 3 = 3.0 times or more, or 4.0 mg/dL or more, or renal replacement started (or, under 18, eGFR under 35). KDIGO gives no rule for a missing baseline; Agere's convention (state it) is the lowest result in the prior 7 days. With dates only (no times), 48 hours is approximated by results up to 2 days apart; say so. A coded diagnosis of AKI is ICD-10-CM N17.

retrieves: How many patients had acute kidney injury by creatinine in 2028?
AKI events by lab criteria
ignores: How many patients had a creatinine test in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM measurement a JOIN measurement b ON a.patient_id = b.patient_id WHERE a.concept = 'creatinine' AND b.concept = 'creatinine' AND b.value_canonical - a.value_canonical >= 0.3
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'creatinine' AND value_canonical > 1.2
tests.check_question: How many patients had acute kidney injury by creatinine in 2028?

concepts.name: Diabetes and prediabetes by HbA1c and glucose (ADA)
concepts.triggers: undiagnosed diabetes|prediabet|pre-diabet|diabetic range|meets? (?:the )?(?:criteria|definition) for diabetes|diabetes (?:by|on) (?:lab|a1c|hba1c|glucose)|could have diabetes|likely diabet
concepts.summary: ADA diagnostic thresholds: diabetes is HbA1c 6.5% or more, fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL or more, 2-hour glucose 200 mg/dL or more on an oral glucose tolerance test, or a random glucose 200 mg/dL or more with classic symptoms or a hyperglycemic crisis. Otherwise two abnormal results are needed: two different tests (which may be from the same sample) or the same test on two occasions. Prediabetes is HbA1c 5.7-6.4%, fasting glucose 100-125 mg/dL, or 2-hour OGTT glucose 140-199 mg/dL. A random (non-fasting) glucose below 200 does not diagnose anything; lab tables usually do not say whether a glucose was fasting. 'Undiagnosed diabetes' means a diabetic-range result in a patient with no diabetes diagnosis on record (ICD-10-CM E08-E13).

retrieves: How many patients have an HbA1c in the diabetic range but no diabetes diagnosis?
How many patients have prediabetes by A1c?
ignores: How many patients filled metformin in 2028?

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'hba1c' AND value_canonical >= 7
tests.check_question: How many patients have undiagnosed diabetes?

concepts.name: Hypoglycemia levels (ADA)
concepts.summary: ADA hypoglycemia levels: level 1 is glucose under 70 mg/dL and at or above 54; level 2 (clinically significant) is under 54 mg/dL; level 3 is a severe event needing another person's help, with no glucose threshold. 'Hypoglycemia' by lab means glucose under 70 mg/dL unless a level is named. Coded hypoglycemia: ICD-10-CM E16.0-E16.2 and E10.64x, E11.64x, E13.64x (.641 with coma, .649 without).

retrieves: How many patients had a hypoglycemic glucose result in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'glucose' AND value_canonical < 70
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'glucose' AND value_canonical < 80
tests.check_question: How many patients had hypoglycemia by lab in 2028?

concepts.name: CMS122 glycemic status above 9% (poor control)
concepts.triggers: poor(?:ly)? (?:glycemic )?control|uncontrolled diabet|a1c (?:over|above|greater than|>) ?9|hba1c (?:over|above|greater than|>) ?9|cms ?122|glycemic status|diabetes control
concepts.summary: CMS122 (inverse measure; lower is better): patients 18-75 by the end of the measurement period with diabetes and a visit in the period. Numerator: the most recent glycemic status assessment in the period (HbA1c or GMI, as %) is above 9.0%, or is missing, or none was done; a patient with no result in the year counts as poorly controlled. If several results share the latest date, use the lowest. Exclusions: hospice or palliative care during the period; age 66 and older living long term in a nursing home; age 66 and older with frailty plus advanced illness or dementia medication (period or prior year). 'Above 9' is strictly greater than 9.0.

retrieves: What share of our diabetic patients are poorly controlled (A1c over 9) in 2028?
CMS122 rate for 2028

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'hba1c' AND value_canonical > 8

concepts.name: Blood pressure categories (2017 ACC/AHA)
concepts.triggers: stage [12] hypertension|elevated blood pressure|blood pressure categor|hypertensive (?:urgency|crisis|emergency)|severe(?:ly)? (?:high|elevated) (?:blood pressure|bp)|severe hypertension|\bbp (?:of|over|above) 1[4-8]0|blood pressure (?:of|over|above) 1[4-8]0
concepts.summary: 2017 ACC/AHA adult categories (mmHg), based on the average of two or more readings on two or more occasions: normal under 120 and under 80; elevated 120-129 and under 80; stage 1 hypertension 130-139 or 80-89; stage 2 hypertension 140 or more or 90 or more. When systolic and diastolic fall in different categories, use the higher. Hypertensive crisis is BP over 180 systolic and/or over 120 diastolic: an emergency if there is new or worsening target-organ damage, an urgency if not. A single reading in a range is a reading, not a diagnosis.

concepts.name: CMS165 controlling high blood pressure
concepts.triggers: controll?(?:ed|ing) (?:high )?(?:blood pressure|bp|hypertension)|blood pressure control|bp control|cms ?165|hypertension (?:is |are )?(?:controlled|under control)|uncontrolled (?:hypertension|blood pressure|bp)
concepts.summary: CMS165: patients 18-85 by the end of the year with essential hypertension starting before and continuing into, or starting in the first six months of, the year, and a visit in the year. Numerator: the most recent blood pressure in the year is adequately controlled, systolic under 140 AND diastolic under 90. When several readings share the most recent date, use the lowest systolic and the lowest diastolic of that day. Readings from acute inpatient stays or ED visits do not count, both a systolic and a diastolic value are required (ranges do not count), and patient-reported readings from automated devices are accepted. No reading in the year counts as not controlled. Exclusions: hospice or palliative care in the year; ESRD, dialysis or kidney transplant before or during the year; pregnancy in the year; age 66 or older living long-term in a nursing home; age 66-80 with frailty plus advanced illness or dementia medication (this year or last); age 81 or older with frailty.

sources.where: Initial population, numerator guidance on multiple same-day readings, exclusions

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'systolic_bp' AND value_canonical < 130

concepts.name: Severe hypercholesterolemia (LDL 190 or more)
concepts.summary: 2018 AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline: an LDL cholesterol of 190 mg/dL (4.9 mmol/L) or more is severe primary hypercholesterolemia; start a high-intensity statin without calculating 10-year ASCVD risk. CMS347 applies this group to ages 20-75. 'LDL of 190 or more' includes 190.

concepts.name: CMS347 statin therapy benefit groups
concepts.triggers: statin benefit|should be on a statin|eligible for (?:a )?statin|statin therapy for (?:the )?prevention|cms ?347|statin gap|missing (?:a )?statin
concepts.summary: CMS347 (v8, 2025) counts patients in any of four groups who were taking or were prescribed a statin in the year: (1) clinical ASCVD (acute coronary syndrome, prior MI, stable or unstable angina, coronary or other arterial revascularization, stroke or TIA, atherosclerotic peripheral arterial disease), any age; (2) age 20-75 with any LDL-C of 190 mg/dL or more ever, or familial hypercholesterolemia; (3) age 40-75 with type 1 or type 2 diabetes; (4) age 40-75 with a 10-year ASCVD risk of 20% or more. A qualifying encounter is required. Denominator exclusions: breastfeeding and rhabdomyolysis. Denominator exceptions: statin-associated muscle symptoms or statin allergy, palliative or hospice care, active liver disease or hepatic insufficiency, ESRD, or a documented medical reason. Adherence and intensity are not scored.

retrieves: How many patients eligible for a statin under CMS347 have no statin fill in 2028?

concepts.name: HFrEF and guideline-directed medical therapy (four classes)
concepts.triggers: \bgdmt\b|guideline[- ]directed|hfref|reduced ejection fraction|reduced ef|four pillars|quadruple therapy|optimal medical therapy for heart failure
concepts.summary: HFrEF is heart failure with LVEF 40% or less (2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA). Guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF is four classes: (1) a renin-angiotensin inhibitor: ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) recommended in NYHA class II-III, an ACE inhibitor when ARNI is not feasible, or an ARB when the ACE inhibitor is not tolerated; (2) an evidence-based beta blocker: carvedilol, metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol only (other beta blockers do not count); (3) a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone, eplerenone); (4) an SGLT2 inhibitor (class recommendation; dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are the dosed agents). 'On GDMT' means all four classes (the guideline's 'all 4 drug classes'); say if a looser count is used. Patients with improved EF (previous HFrEF, now LVEF above 40%) stay on HFrEF therapy. Coded HFrEF is ICD-10-CM I50.2x (systolic) or I50.4x (combined).

sources.where: Section 7.3, stage C HFrEF pharmacological treatment

retrieves: How many HFrEF patients are on all four GDMT classes?
patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction on guideline-directed therapy
ignores: How many heart failure admissions in 2028?

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM fill WHERE drug_class = 'beta_blocker'
tests.check_question: How many HFrEF patients are on GDMT?

concepts.name: Natriuretic peptide thresholds for heart failure (ESC)
concepts.summary: 2021 ESC: heart failure is unlikely in a non-acute setting with NT-proBNP under 125 pg/mL (BNP under 35); in an acute setting the rule-out is NT-proBNP under 300 pg/mL (BNP under 100). These are rule-out thresholds: values above them are not diagnostic of heart failure (natriuretic peptides rise in other cardiac and non-cardiac conditions and can be low in obesity). 'Elevated NT-proBNP' therefore means 125 pg/mL or more out of hospital, 300 or more in acute care; say which.

retrieves: How many patients had an elevated NT-proBNP in 2028?
ignores: How many patients had a troponin test?

concepts.name: Iron deficiency (general and in heart failure)
concepts.summary: In heart failure (2021 ESC) iron deficiency is ferritin under 100 ng/mL, or ferritin 100-299 ng/mL with transferrin saturation (TSAT) under 20%; inflammation raises ferritin. Outside heart failure the cutoffs differ by source and no outside-HF source is in the store yet: state the cutoff used. TSAT is LOINC 2502-3 (iron / total iron-binding capacity).

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'ferritin' AND value_canonical < 30
tests.check_question: How many heart failure patients are iron deficient?

concepts.name: Anaemia by haemoglobin (WHO adult cutoffs)
concepts.summary: WHO 2024 cutoffs: anaemia is haemoglobin under 13.0 g/dL in men and under 12.0 g/dL in non-pregnant women, ages 15-65, at sea level (the guideline adjusts for elevation and smoking). WHO gives no separate cutoff above 65 and lists older adults as a research gap; applying the 15-65 cutoffs to older adults is an assumption to state. The cutoff depends on sex: a single cutoff for everyone is wrong. Severity (non-pregnant adults): mild 11.0 to just under the cutoff, moderate 8.0-10.9, severe under 8.0 g/dL. A coded anaemia diagnosis is ICD-10-CM D50-D64 (sickle-cell trait D57.3 is not anaemia; thalassaemia minor and pancytopenia codes often are not).

retrieves: How many patients were anemic by hemoglobin in 2028?
ignores: How many patients had a platelet count?

check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'hemoglobin' AND value_canonical < 12

concepts.name: Hyperkalaemia thresholds (sources differ)
concepts.summary: Sources differ on the threshold. The KDIGO controversies conference (2020) defines hyperkalaemia as potassium above the laboratory upper limit of normal; its severity grid starts at 5.0 mmol/L (or the upper limit of normal): 5.0-5.9 mild, 6.0-6.4 moderate, 6.5 or more severe, each moved up one level with ECG changes. The European Resuscitation Council (2021) is reported to use 5.5 mmol/L as the threshold (not yet confirmed against its text). When a question says 'hyperkalemia' without a number and no customer definition settles it, the two cutoffs are two readings: ask which, or give both.

retrieves: How many patients had hyperkalemia in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'potassium' AND value_canonical > 5.0
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM measurement WHERE concept = 'potassium' AND value_canonical > 6
tests.check_question: How many patients had hyperkalemia in 2028?

concepts.summary: European clinical practice guideline (2014): hyponatraemia is serum sodium under 135 mmol/L measured by ion-specific electrode; mild 130 to under 135, moderate 125-129, profound under 125 mmol/L. Coded hyponatraemia is ICD-10-CM E87.1.

concepts.name: Sepsis: Sepsis-3, SIRS and coded sepsis
concepts.summary: Sepsis-3 (2016): life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated host response to infection, operationalised as suspected infection plus an acute rise in SOFA score of 2 or more (baseline SOFA may be assumed zero without known organ dysfunction); septic shock is sepsis needing vasopressors to keep mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg or more with lactate above 2 mmol/L despite adequate fluids. SIRS (1992): two or more of temperature over 38 or under 36 C, heart rate over 90, respiratory rate over 20 (or PaCO2 under 32 mmHg), white count over 12 or under 4 x10^3/uL (or over 10% bands). SEP-1 uses a modified SIRS: temperature over 38.3 or under 36.0 C, heart rate over 90, respiratory rate over 20 (no PaCO2 criterion), white count over 12 or under 4 or over 10% bands, with separate thresholds in pregnancy. SOFA needs PaO2/FiO2, platelets, bilirubin, vasopressors, Glasgow score and creatinine or urine output; most warehouses cannot compute it. Sepsis-3 recommends R65.20/R65.21 as primary ICD-10 codes and, for data, identifies suspected infection by a body-fluid culture plus antibiotics within a set window; A40, A41 and the organism-specific sepsis codes are a broader coded proxy (our choice, not Sepsis-3's).

not_computable.needs: SOFA components (PaO2/FiO2, bilirubin, vasopressor doses, Glasgow Coma Scale, urine output) with times; the warehouse has none of the respiratory, neurological or vasopressor parts

sources.where: criteria as reproduced in Sepsis-3 Box 1

concepts.name: Lactate thresholds in sepsis (SEP-1, Sepsis-3)
concepts.summary: Lactate is reported in mmol/L. SEP-1: a lactate above 2 mmol/L is a sign of organ dysfunction for severe sepsis, and an initial lactate above 2 calls for a repeat lactate (within 6 hours of severe sepsis presentation per older specifications; confirm the current manual); initial hypotension or a lactate of 4 mmol/L or more (septic shock) requires 30 mL/kg crystalloid (a lesser documented volume with a reason is accepted). Sepsis-3 septic shock uses lactate above 2 mmol/L. 'Elevated lactate' means above 2 mmol/L unless 4 or more is named. In lab tables lactate is LOINC 2524-7 (serum or plasma), 32693-4 (blood), 2518-9 (arterial), 2519-7 (venous blood) or 32133-1 (venous plasma).

concepts.name: SEP-1 bundle compliance needs times
concepts.triggers: sep-?1|sepsis bundle|bundle complian|time to antibiotic|antibiotics? within (?:1|one|3|three) hours?
concepts.summary: SEP-1 compliance needs the time of severe sepsis presentation and the times of each bundle element: lactate drawn, blood cultures before antibiotics, broad-spectrum antibiotics, a repeat lactate within 6 hours of severe sepsis presentation if the initial lactate was above 2; for septic shock, 30 mL/kg crystalloid within 3 hours, and vasopressors for persistent hypotension and a repeat volume status and perfusion assessment within 6 hours of shock presentation. The denominator is inpatients 18 and older with a sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock code. It is abstracted from charts. Without order and administration times it cannot be computed.

concepts.name: NHSN device-associated infections (CAUTI, CLABSI) need device days and cultures
concepts.summary: NHSN CAUTI and CLABSI are surveillance definitions, not diagnosis codes. CAUTI: an indwelling urethral catheter (not suprapubic or straight) in place more than 2 consecutive days in an inpatient location and still in place on the date of event or the day before; a urine culture with no more than two species, at least one a bacterium at 100,000 CFU/mL or more (yeasts alone do not count); and symptoms (symptomatic UTI) or a blood culture matching the urine organism (asymptomatic bacteremic UTI). Rates are per 1,000 device days counted by calendar day; the standardized infection ratio (SIR) divides observed by NHSN-predicted infections. CLABSI needs central line days and blood culture rules (pathogen versus common commensal). Without device days, culture results and NHSN predicted counts it cannot be computed.

not_computable.needs: device days (urinary catheter or central line), culture results with organisms and dates, and NHSN predicted counts; the warehouse has none of them

concepts.name: Potentially inappropriate medications in older adults (AGS Beers 2023, selected classes)
concepts.summary: The AGS Beers Criteria (2023) list medications that adults 65 and older (outside hospice and end-of-life care) should generally avoid. Classes the warehouse can see by drug class include: benzodiazepines; first-generation antihistamines; skeletal muscle relaxants (not those used for spasticity); sulfonylureas (avoid as first- or second-line monotherapy or add-on therapy); chronic use of oral non-COX-2-selective NSAIDs unless alternatives are not effective and a gastroprotective agent can be taken; scheduled proton pump inhibitor use beyond 8 weeks unless high risk or another listed indication; antipsychotics except FDA-approved indications such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, Parkinson disease psychosis, adjunctive treatment of major depression or short-term antiemetic use. Beers is criteria, not a single measure: name which classes are counted. Here age is taken as 65 or older at the fill date (our rule).

concepts.name: Concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine use
concepts.summary: FDA (2016) added boxed warnings to opioid pain and cough medicines and to benzodiazepines because combining them can cause slowed or difficult breathing, sedation and death; it advises limiting co-prescribing to patients without adequate alternatives. CDC's 2022 guideline (Recommendation 11) says to use particular caution when prescribing them together. Concurrent use means the days' supply of an opioid fill and a benzodiazepine fill overlap (here each fill covers fill date through fill date plus days supplied minus 1). The PQA COB measure (a CMS Part D Star Ratings measure from 2027, measurement year 2025) is stricter: beneficiaries 18 and older with 2 or more opioid claims on different dates and 15 or more days' opioid supply (denominator), counted when they also have 2 or more benzodiazepine claims on different dates and 30 or more cumulative days of overlapping supply; hospice, palliative care, cancer, cancer-related pain treatment and sickle cell disease are excluded. Overlap of any day and the COB measure are two readings; say which.

readings.label: any day of overlapping supply
readings.rule: supplies overlap by at least one day

readings.label: PQA/CMS COB: 2+ opioid claims and 15+ opioid days, 2+ benzodiazepine claims, 30+ days of overlap

retrieves: How many patients had overlapping opioid and benzodiazepine prescriptions in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.patient_id) FROM fill a JOIN fill b ON a.patient_id = b.patient_id WHERE a.drug_class = 'opioid' AND b.drug_class = 'benzodiazepine' AND a.fill_date <= b.supply_end AND b.fill_date <= a.supply_end
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.patient_id) FROM fill a JOIN fill b ON a.patient_id = b.patient_id WHERE a.drug_class = 'opioid' AND b.drug_class = 'benzodiazepine' AND substr(a.fill_date,1,4) = substr(b.fill_date,1,4)
tests.check_question: How many patients had concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine use in 2028?

concepts.name: 'Triple whammy': NSAID with a RAS blocker and a diuretic
concepts.summary: The 'triple whammy' is concurrent use of an NSAID, an ACE inhibitor or ARB, and a diuretic. In a nested case-control study of UK antihypertensive users (Lapi 2013), current triple therapy was associated with a 31% higher rate of acute kidney injury (rate ratio 1.31, 95% CI 1.12-1.53), highest in the first 30 days (1.82, 1.35-2.46). The study counted drugs as concurrent when prescribed the same day or when their supplies overlapped by at least one day. Here supply runs from the fill date through fill date plus days supplied minus 1. Lapi did not split diuretics by type; counting loop and thiazide diuretics, and leaving out potassium-sparing MRAs unless the question asks, is our rule.

retrieves: How many patients were on a triple whammy combination in 2028?
check_passes: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT n.patient_id) FROM fill n JOIN fill r ON r.patient_id = n.patient_id AND r.drug_class IN ('ace_inhibitor','arb') JOIN fill d ON d.patient_id = n.patient_id AND d.drug_class IN ('loop_diuretic','thiazide_diuretic') WHERE n.drug_class = 'nsaid' AND n.fill_date <= r.supply_end AND r.fill_date <= n.supply_end
check_fails: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM fill WHERE drug_class = 'nsaid'
tests.check_question: How many patients were on a triple whammy combination in 2028?

concepts.name: Metformin and reduced eGFR (FDA)
concepts.summary: FDA (2016): kidney function for metformin is judged by eGFR, not serum creatinine, checked before starting and at least yearly; metformin is contraindicated with eGFR under 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, starting it at 30-45 is not recommended, and the benefit should be reassessed if eGFR falls below 45 (these thresholds not yet confirmed against FDA's text); stop it before iodinated contrast when eGFR is 30-60. KDIGO 2022 (PP 4.1.3) separately advises adjusting the dose below eGFR 45. Agere's operational rule (not FDA's): 'on metformin with eGFR under 30' means a metformin supply covering a date on or after an eGFR under 30, or a fill after it.

concepts.name: Atrial fibrillation and oral anticoagulation
concepts.summary: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS: oral anticoagulation is recommended for atrial fibrillation with an annual thromboembolic risk of 2% or more (for example CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more in men, 3 or more in women; other validated scores are allowed), and is reasonable at 1% to under 2%. Direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban) are preferred over warfarin except in moderate-to-severe rheumatic mitral stenosis or with a mechanical heart valve. Coded atrial fibrillation is ICD-10-CM I48.0, I48.1x, I48.2x and I48.91; I48.3, I48.4 and I48.92 are atrial flutter.

concepts.name: AHRQ PQI 08 heart failure admission rate
concepts.summary: AHRQ Prevention Quality Indicators (v2024) are area-level rates: admissions per 100,000 residents aged 18 and older of a county or metro area, assigned by patient residence. PQI 01 (diabetes short-term complications): principal diagnosis of type 1, type 2 or other specified diabetes with ketoacidosis, hyperosmolarity or coma (including hypoglycemic coma), excluding transfers. The software reports a rate per person; multiply by 100,000. The denominator is the resident adult population, not admitted or enrolled patients; a health system's enrolled members are a stated substitute.

concepts.name: Polypharmacy (definitions vary)
concepts.summary: A systematic review (Masnoon 2017) found the most common definition of polypharmacy is five or more medications daily (46.4% of studies; definitions ranged from two or more to 11 or more). Ten or more was labelled 'excessive polypharmacy' in some studies, and 'hyperpolypharmacy' or 'severe polypharmacy' in single studies. Most definitions are simple counts; a minority add a duration of therapy or a care setting, and only one study counted drug classes rather than drugs. Count concurrent supplies (overlapping days' supply) of distinct drugs or classes, and say which.
